title: Waitresses, river-boat bands and Eddie Inge's offer of a Milwaukee job
summary: Waitresses wondered why the trumpeter never came upstairs; Eddie Inge, who had been watching him, phoned from Milwaukee with a Roof Garden job.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Were some of the St. Louis men playing on river boats at that time?

We had a fellow on piano by the name of Burroughs Lovingood. Yeah. Burroughs Lovingood. We sent and got Lovingood from there. Well, I can tell you about that a little later on. So, I played there for awhile. It's a funny thing, though, while I was there, while I was studying, when I was at the Chauffeur's Club. Boy, they had some beautiful waitresses -- very beautiful girls, and they couldn't understand why all the boys would be up there buying those club sandwiches and setting the waitresses up and why is it Randolph don't come up here?

What's the matter that you all hate the trumpet player? Why does he -- why is it that he didn't come up here? They say, "Well, he's sitting back out there building air castles." That's what they were saying. I was studying at this time. This was before Hudson had told me that -- I had -- he had given me all he could -- had exhausted his vocabulary or what have you. So, I played fair and went on and on until a fellow by the name of Chauffeur Inge came to Chauffeur's Club and I wondered why he kept a hanging around and listening and looking, and I noticed he looked at me and he kept looking at me and listening. Every time I'd go to play, he'd -- I wondered, I said, "I wonder what gives with the fellow?" But he wouldn't -- he didn't say anything to me. So, finally, on the last time, this guy asked me if I'd like to -- if I'd take a job on the Roof Garden. And I told him, I said, "Oh, yes, I'll take the job, sure. I'll take the job on the Roof Garden." So, finally, one time -- one Sunday night he called me up and said, "This is Eddie Inge." He says, "I'm calling from Milwaukee." He says, "Do you want this job?" I says, "Yes." He says, "Well, I told the man about you and he says if you come up here you can get this job." I said, "Tell him you know what I'm going to tell him now. (unintelligible). Tell him to send me a ticket." So, he sent me the ticket. And then I put my notice in and I went to Milwaukee.
